dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:301.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:302.text: Licorice, 甘艸. Formed from 艸 and 甘.

shuowen:303.text: A plant that can be made into rope. Formed from 艸, with 予 indicating the sound.

shuowen:304.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 盡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:305.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 述 indicating the sound.

shuowen:306.text: The plant 荵冬. Formed from 艸, with 忍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:307.text: 萇楚, namely 跳弋; also called 羊桃. Formed from 艸, with 長 indicating the sound.

shuowen:308.text: The plant 芺. Formed from 艸, with 魝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:309.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 里 indicating the sound. Read like 釐.

shuowen:310.text: The plant 釐艸. Another explanation: 拜商藋. Formed from 艸, with 翟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:311.text: The plant 堇艸. Formed from 艸, with 及 indicating the sound. Read like 急.

shuowen:312.text: Mountain 苺. Formed from 艸, with 歬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:313.text: A poisonous plant. Formed from 艸, with 婺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:314.text: The plant 卷耳. Formed from 艸, with 務 indicating the sound.

shuowen:315.text: Ginseng, 人薓, a medicinal plant from Shangdang. Formed from 艸, with 𣹰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:316.text: The plant 鳧葵. Formed from 艸, with 攣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:317.text: A plant that can dye a yellow called 留黃. Formed from 艸, with 戾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:318.text: The plant 蚍𧉈. Formed from 艸, with 收 indicating the sound.

shuowen:319.text: Mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 毗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:320.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 禹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:321.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 夷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:322.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 辥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:323.text: 大苦, namely 苓. Formed from 艸, with 古 indicating the sound.

shuowen:324.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 咅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:325.text: The plant 薏苢 (Job’s tears). Formed from 艸, with 𠶷 indicating the sound. An alternative name is 𦺳英.

shuowen:326.text: The grass 菅. Formed from 艸, with 矛 indicating the sound.

shuowen:327.text: The grass 茅. Formed from 艸, with 官 indicating the sound.

shuowen:328.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 纥 indicating the sound. Jiangxia has a Qichun station.

shuowen:329.text: A plant that can be made into mats. Formed from 艸, with 完 indicating the sound.

shuowen:330.text: A kind of 莞. Formed from 艸, with 閵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:331.text: 黃蒢, namely 職. Formed from 艸, with 除 indicating the sound.

shuowen:332.text: An aquatic plant that can be made into mats. Formed from 艸, with 浦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:333.text: Young 蒲 shoots, which can be made into flat mats. Formed from 艸, with 弱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:334.text: A kind of 蒲 or 蒻. Formed from 艸, with 深 indicating the sound.

shuowen:335.text: The plant 萑. Formed from 艸, with 推 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “In the valley there is 蓷.”

shuowen:336.text: The appearance of abundant plants. Formed from 艸, with 隹 indicating the sound.

shuowen:337.text: The plant 缺盆. Formed from 艸, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:338.text: Well weed, 井藻. Formed from 艸, with 君 indicating the sound. Read like 威.

shuowen:339.text: The plant 夫蘺. Formed from 艸, with 睆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:340.text: The top of 夫蘺. Formed from 艸, with 鬲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:341.text: 芣苢, also called 馬舄. Its fruit resembles a plum and promotes childbearing. Formed from 艸, with 㠯 indicating the sound. This is the account in the Book of Zhou.

shuowen:342.text: The plant 䒞藩. Formed from 艸, with 尋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:343.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 毄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:344.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 區 indicating the sound.

shuowen:345.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 固 indicating the sound.

shuowen:346.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 榦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:347.text: Sugarcane, 藷蔗. Formed from 艸, with 諸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:348.text: Sugarcane, 藷蔗. Formed from 艸, with 庶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:349.text: 牂𧃱, which can be made into cords and well ropes. Formed from 艸, with 𤕦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:350.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 賜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:351.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 中 indicating the sound.

shuowen:352.text: The plant 王萯. Formed from 艸, with 負 indicating the sound.

shuowen:353.text: A bitter-tasting plant, eaten south of the Yangtze to bring down qi. Formed from 艸, with 夭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:354.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 弦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:355.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 𡈹 indicating the sound. 𡈹 is the large-seal form of 囿.

shuowen:356.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 孚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:357.text: The plant 兎苽. Formed from 艸, with 寅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:358.text: The plant 馬帚. Formed from 艸, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:359.text: A plant growing beside water. Formed from 艸, with 猶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:360.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 安 indicating the sound.

shuowen:361.text: An edible fern-like plant called 紫藄 or 月爾, identified in a traditional commentary as a purple fern. Formed from 艸, with 綦 indicating the sound. [Duan proposes a substantially different ancient gloss 士夫也; the received text is disputed.]

shuowen:362.text: The plant 兎葵. Formed from 艸, with abbreviated 稀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:363.text: The plant 灌渝. Formed from 艸, with 夢 indicating the sound. Read like 萌.

shuowen:364.text: The plant 盜庚. Formed from 艸, with 復 indicating the sound.

shuowen:365.text: The plant 卷耳. Formed from 艸, with 令 indicating the sound.

shuowen:366.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 𥫔 indicating the sound. Another explanation: 薏苢.

shuowen:367.text: A grass-like plant identified as 藑茅, belonging to the 葍 group. Formed from 艸, with 夐 indicating the sound. [The received alternative name 蕣 is challenged by Duan Yucai.]

shuowen:368.text: The plant 葍. Formed from 艸, with 富 indicating the sound.

shuowen:369.text: The plant 䔰. Formed from 艸, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:370.text: A seedling. Formed from 艸, with 脩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:371.text: The plant 蓨. Formed from 艸, with 由 indicating the sound.

shuowen:372.text: A plant whose branches meet branch to branch and leaves face leaf to leaf. Formed from 艸, with 昜 indicating the sound.

shuowen:373.text: The plant 嬰薁. Formed from 艸, with 奥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:374.text: The plant 馬藍. Formed from 艸, with 咸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:375.text: A plant usable for binding. Formed from 艸, with 魯 indicating the sound.

shuowen:376.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 㕟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:377.text: A plant usable in cooking fish. Formed from 艸, with 婁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:378.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 畾 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Luxuriant are the kudzu and 藟.” Another explanation: black millet for sacrificial wine.

shuowen:379.text: The plant 棘蒬. Formed from 艸, with 冤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:380.text: The plant 茈艸. Formed from 艸, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:381.text: The plant 茈艸. Formed from 艸, with 䫉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:382.text: The plant 烏喙. Formed from 艸, with 則 indicating the sound.

shuowen:383.text: 茅蒐, namely 茹藘, madder. It grows from human blood and can dye deep red. Formed from 艸 and 鬼.

shuowen:384.text: The plant 茅蒐. Formed from 艸, with 西 indicating the sound.

shuowen:385.text: The plant 赤𧀳. Formed from 艸 and 𨽸.

shuowen:386.text: The plant 牡贊. Formed from 艸, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:387.text: The plant 杜榮. Formed from 艸, with 忘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:388.text: A plant used in Nanyang to make coarse sandals. Formed from 艸, with 包 indicating the sound.

shuowen:389.text: The plant 冰臺, mugwort. Formed from 艸, with 乂 indicating the sound.

shuowen:390.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 章 indicating the sound.

shuowen:391.text: The plant 楚葵. Formed from 艸, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:392.text: The plant 豕首. Formed from 艸, with 甄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:393.text: A parasitic plant. Formed from 艸, with 鳥 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “蔦 and 女蘿.”

shuowen:394.text: A plant resembling 目宿. Formed from 艸, with 云 indicating the sound. The Huainanzi says: “芸 grass can die and come to life again.”

shuowen:395.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 𠭥 indicating the sound.

shuowen:396.text: A plant. Formed from 艸, with 律 indicating the sound.

shuowen:397.text: A thorn. Formed from 艸, with 朿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:398.text: The plant 䒷婁 (also 栝樓/瓜蔞), a gourd-bearing climbing vine. Formed from 艸, with 𠯑 indicating the sound.

shuowen:399.text: The plant 須從. Formed from 艸, with 封 indicating the sound.

shuowen:400.text: The plant 蒺棃. Formed from 艸, with 齊 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “There is 薺 on the wall.”
